overview.text: The Red Diamond Rattlesnake is a venomous rattlesnake of south-western California and Baja California, named for its reddish colour.

identification.text: Looks like the Western Diamond-backed Rattlesnake, but reddish in colour, with a pattern of diamonds down the back and a rattle on the tail.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Commonly over 100 cm on the mainland; large males over 140 cm. The record is 162 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-western California and the Baja California peninsula, plus islands in the Gulf of California.

habitat.text: Dense chaparral in the foothills, cactus patches and brushy boulders, from sea level to about 1,500 m.

diet.text: Rabbits, ground squirrels, birds, lizards and other snakes.

reproduction.text: Mates from February to April and gives birth to 3 to 20 live young in August, each 30 to 34 cm long.
